reviews.author: Yongchan Kim
reviews.text: It was a franchise restaurant I had seen many times before, so I decided to visit. Even though it was a Saturday afternoon, it was full of customers. I ordered the signature dish, raw pork belly (13,000 won per serving), and side dishes of raw cold noodles and lunch box bibimbap. The meat you order is first grilled in the kitchen and then grilled by the waiter to make it suitable for eating. Aged kimchi is cooked together, and if you eat it with meat, the sourness of the kimchi goes well with the juiciness of the meat, making it very flavorful. Or, it is delicious eaten with green vegetables or lettuce. The meat seemed to be slightly seasoned and the meat itself was delicious, perhaps because it had been aged. The lunch box bibimbap was a bit bland. However, I feel like the portion size for each menu item is a bit small. One serving of raw pork belly was 180g, and the raw cold noodles and bibimbap seemed small at first glance. The price is not very expensive, but for those who purchase large quantities, additional orders and costs may be necessary. What was unique was that it was a drinking glass for wheat. It seems to have been manufactured by a liquor company, but it was a good idea product made perfectly for wheat.

It does not have a strong smell and is soft like beef because it is lamb, but because the legs are served whole, there are chewy and soft parts in each part and you can eat them differently. There is a reason why Konkuk University Lamb Legs is famous for its barbecue.

At first, they cut just enough pieces to be grilled and put them on the grill, but if you find it difficult to grill by yourself with a knife, you can ask the staff and they will cut it into bite-sized pieces and bring it to you. I cut it into small pieces on my own, so I asked for it while doing it myself hahahaha.

The owner also taught me how to eat it very deliciously. Like dipping it in onion jjangajji and topping it with onions and eating it together?! It's super delicious!!!

The satire explained it as the red kewobaroo that he mentioned on YouTube, and it's really my style. This kwaebarou tastes sweeter than the sour red sauce, and it's the perfect dish to eat in between legs of lamb!!! I thought it was a good idea to order it together. reviews.text:
The best cost-effective ramen restaurant near Konkuk University

These days, Japanese food prices, which are nothing special, have become seriously expensive under the pretext of foreign food, but I am very grateful that they maintain reasonable prices.
Just because it's good cost-effectiveness doesn't mean it's not tasty. It's not too Japanese-style, and it's just delicious enough to suit Korean tastes.
You can choose the noodles, and the thick noodles are chewy. It's also nice that adding a cotton sari is free.

However, it is not all good and is very disappointing in terms of internal hygiene.
There's so much mold or something dark in the corner that it's unpleasant and humid, and the table gets sticky every time I go.
I would like to give it 5 stars because it is good value for money and suits my Korean palate rather than Japanese food that boasts extreme saltiness like an authentic Japanese restaurant, but unfortunately I can't do that due to hygiene reasons.

If it were a shabby house run by an old man, I would understand because he couldn't afford it, but he doesn't look old here and I don't know why he can't do that while working part-time. I would like to install a dehumidifier for humid areas and clean moldy areas more often after changing the wallpaper.
Oh, and this is a chronic problem in many Japanese restaurants these days, so I think it's time for this restaurant to change their chopsticks too.
Since Japanese chopsticks are not made of metal, they wear out quickly, but at the same time, they are not that expensive, so I don't know why people don't replace them.
If you notice that your dishes are showing signs of wear, change them often.
Because this is also connected to hygiene.

When I went there recently, I was a little confused because I guess it was a part-time job and they immediately responded in Japanese.
Afterwards, orders were taken in Korean, but I could tell you were speaking slurred, so I guess you were Japanese? Or it seemed like he was a foreigner.
Well, it's not a big problem, but maybe it's a characteristic of Konkuk University's selection of people.. No matter how part-time it is, I think they should at least select people who are good at Korean.

But I think I left a review here too, why isn't there one?

The amount of green onions, garlic, and bean sprouts can be adjusted to your desired level.

Also, three types of noodles are added for free, so don't worry if you have a lot of noodles.

If you are considering additional noodles, you can enjoy Butanchu's ramen even more deliciously by adding Hosomen, which cooks the fastest, and choosing Chiji Ramen or Dragon Men, which cook at a slower rate, when ordering for the first time.

Char siu and soft-boiled egg (ajitamago) are also attractive, so it's a good idea to eat them together.

Much better than places like Aori... I really wish they would open a branch near the company...

The dumplings we used to eat together seem to have disappeared...
It's a pity...

Maybe because I went in the evening, I didn't have to wait in line, but it was quiet inside.

Has the number of people decreased significantly?

I highly recommend it.

reviews.author: A house that only tastes good
reviews.text:
A restaurant specializing in ramen

Walk for about 10 minutes from Exit 2 of Konkuk University Station.
This ramen restaurant can be found on the second floor inside an alley.
You can eat tonkotsu ramen for 10,000 won.
I sprinkled a lot of sesame seeds before taking the picture.
The standard ramen does not have many sesame seeds.
The face has a strange visual.
It seems as if the noodles are hand-picked at the store.
The soup doesn't have a strong porky smell.
In general, there is no inconvenience in eating, but
For my taste buds, it feels a bit bland.
The chashu that comes as a garnish isn’t bad.
The eggs felt like soft-boiled eggs.
The yolk is cloudy like water and has a unique scent.
People who can't eat soft-boiled food may find it fishy because they can taste it.
Among the ajitamago I've ever eaten,
The yolk feels the most watery.
You can buy rice for 1,000 won, but it’s sold out.
It's a bit disappointing that I couldn't eat it with rice.

The store was recently renovated
It's clean and only has counter seats.
It's pretty good for eating alone.
Order and pay at the kiosk at the entrance.
Just sit down and eat where you are guided.
I visited around 8pm on a weekday and it was relatively quiet.
Because it is an open kitchen, you can see the kitchen well.
Wearing gloves is good, but that's one thing.
I'm a little concerned about doing too many things.
Especially touching dishes while doing other things...
When I eat alone, these useless things keep appearing.

Tonkotsu ramen style with less burden~

reviews.author: WOONG’s KITCHEN
reviews.text:
Cho Ramen. Rainy way home from work. I looked for Cho Ramen because I wanted a rich chicken broth. Luckily, I visited when the place was between full and full, so I got in without waiting, ordered tori paitan, and sat down at an empty seat.

The atmosphere was still good. The owner was still passionate and kind, and even though I was alone that day, he was always helpful and organized.

While I was happily melting into the simple, nice atmosphere, the ramen was served to me. A bowl with just the right feel and no flaws. Some people might think it has a bit too much pepper, but for me, who likes pepper, it was perfect for me personally.

Rather, the seasoning was a bit weak compared to the rich and clean broth, so I requested extra tart. The texture of eating kelp and noodles together is good, and the chicken breast, pork belly, and sous vide chashu also have a presence.

At the end, if you roll rice and eat char siu or chive kimchi as a side dish, it feels a bit like a Korean-style samgyetang.

I was able to have a happy evening thanks to the ramen that still suited my taste and the friendly and appropriately energetic energy of the owner. The surprising cost-effectiveness of a university town is a bonus.

reviews.author: Mut Kim
reviews.text: Closing time was 7:30, but when I got there around 6:40, they took my order. I ordered spicy tori paitan and maze soba, and I heard that the level 1 spicy level of tori paitan was about the level of Shin Ramyun, so I decided to level 2 spicy, but it felt like level 2 was level 2 spicy. The noodles were chewy and the soup was thick, so it was good. I think it tasted better when I ate it with rice at the end. Mazesoba was delicious, but it seemed cleaner and tastier after adding kelp vinegar. As expected, the great taste continued until the end even when I mixed it with rice and ate it.

reviews.text: Reservation is required. I had okonomiyaki and shiosoba with pork and squid and it was delicious. reviews.author: Doos Doos
reviews.text:
It was said to be a famous restaurant, but my friend took me to it after saying it had changed to a reservation system. Haha. I often went on business trips to Japan and ate okonomiyaki there often, and it was the same as the local one. (I heard it was a restaurant run by Japanese people, haha)
If I eat okonomiyaki, I will definitely come here.

reviews.author: NU1T
reviews.text:
The 100% reservation system is great.
If you arrive on time, you can eat right away. Even with the one hour limit, I tend to eat slowly, so I have plenty of time. Since it is a reservation system, there are no customers waiting outside, so there is zero stress.

To me, okonomiyaki is a food that I remember for its strong sauce flavor, but this place is surprisingly mild. It seems that the owner was considerate so that you can adjust the sauce to your taste with the sauce provided at the table. Thanks to this, at first I ate it strong(?) with the added sauce, but from about halfway through, I ate it plainly without the sauce, with two flavors.

The overall texture is solid and the vegetables are chewy. Especially the pork belly, grilled very deliciously. Add plenty of katsuobushi.
If you order Yakisoba + Okonomiyaki + a side menu for 2 people, you can leave with your stomach pounding. We resisted ordering one more meal from here, but if we had ordered more, we would have ended up with a waste of food.
I don't drink alcohol, but I really crave highballs.

The interior atmosphere feels like I'm at an old okonomiyaki restaurant somewhere in Japan. It is healing even before eating.
The owner always makes a good impression with a smile on his face, and the staff are also friendly. Please feel free to add more.

Are there any downsides?
does not exist.
